title: Woodpecker Alternatives: 6 Cold Email Tools Compared
summary: Six alternatives to Woodpecker for cold email and LinkedIn outreach, with plan prices, send caps, trial terms and inbox placement testing side by side.
body_markdown:
This page is about Woodpecker the cold email tool at woodpecker.co, and the tools people move to when they outgrow it or want a different pricing model. Whichever tool you land on, start from one test: whether your mail lands in the inbox is part of the campaign, not a separate chore. Warmup, SPF/DKIM/DMARC checks, bounce monitoring and placement tests belong next to the send button, because the alternative is launching to a full list and learning about the spam folder from the silence that follows. Every tool below gets judged on that first, then on price, send caps, LinkedIn, and where your mailboxes come from.


## Who this comparison is for


This is written for a founder or a two-to-five person sales team that runs its own outbound. You have a Woodpecker account or a trial, you send cold email, and you may want LinkedIn steps in the same campaign. You are deciding between flat monthly plans priced on email volume and Woodpecker's model, which prices on the number of people you contact. The per-tool notes are aimed at that smaller team, not at agencies.


## What a Woodpecker replacement has to cover


Woodpecker's pricing page lists its own baseline, so use it as the checklist. Woodpecker includes unlimited email verification, free warm-ups that grow in number as you move up the tiers, unlimited team members and unlimited connected email accounts, a centralized inbox, domain audit, inbox rotation and condition-based campaigns. LinkedIn is an add-on at $29 a month per connected LinkedIn account. A replacement that drops any of those is a step back unless the price makes up for it.


On top of that baseline, five things decide whether the switch is worth it:


1. **Sequences.** Multi-step email with conditional branches, and ideally LinkedIn steps in the same sequence rather than a separate tool.
2. **Warmup.** How many mailboxes warm for free, and what each extra one costs.
3. **Placement testing.** Whether the tool can send a test campaign to seed inboxes and tell you where it landed before you send to real prospects. This is the piece most often sold separately.
4. **One inbox.** All replies from every sending mailbox in one place, with some way of sorting interested replies from out-of-office notes.
5. **Mailbox ownership.** Whether you connect Google or Outlook inboxes you already own, buy domains and mailboxes inside the tool, or both. If you are setting up fresh sending domains either way, our guide to[cold email domains and inboxes setup](https://supersend.io/blog/cold-email-domains-and-inboxes-setup) covers the DNS records and the warmup period before the first send.


The table reads each tool's pricing page on these points. For the same tools judged as a category rather than as Woodpecker replacements, see our guide to the[best cold email software for founders](https://supersend.io/blog/best-cold-email-software) .

## Woodpecker, the baseline


Woodpecker prices on contacted prospects, not emails sent. Its pricing page explains that contacting the same person several times in one campaign counts once toward the limit, and a campaign can run up to 16 steps, so the monthly email allowance is 16 times the prospect count. The slider starts at 500 contacted prospects at $7.00 per 100, which comes to $35 a month, and the rate per prospect drops as you move up. Everything else comes free with the plan: unlimited email verification through Bouncer, a set of free warm-ups that grows with the tier, 100 Lead Finder credits, unlimited team members and unlimited connected mailboxes.


*Woodpecker's pricing page with the contacted-prospects slider, as of October 3, 2026.*


Where the cost grows is in add-ons. Each warmed mailbox beyond the free ones is $5 a month, each LinkedIn account connected is $29 a month, and each Google or Microsoft address bought through Woodpecker is $6 a month. A team that wants three LinkedIn senders and twelve warmed inboxes pays for both on top of the prospect tier. If your sending is steady and your list is small, the prospect model can be cheap. If you send many steps to a large list across many mailboxes, flat volume plans elsewhere are easier to predict, and that is usually why people start reading pages like this one.


## Instantly


Instantly's pricing page splits into Outreach plans, Credits plans for its lead database, and bundles of the two. For a Woodpecker switcher the Outreach plans are the comparable product: Growth at $47 a month gives unlimited email accounts, unlimited warmup, 1,000 uploaded contacts and 5,000 emails a month. Hypergrowth at $97 lifts that to 25,000 uploaded contacts and at least 100,000 emails a month (the plan card says 125,000; the comparison table says 100,000), and Light Speed at $358 adds 500,000 emails, 100,000 contacts and what the page calls the SISR system, which rotates dedicated server and IP blocks for you. Yearly billing lists $37.60, $77.60 and $286.30.


*Instantly's pricing page, as of October 3, 2026.*


The 1,000-contact cap on Growth is the number to watch. Woodpecker counts the people you contact in a month; Instantly caps what you upload. Instantly's Outreach page says campaigns can run email, LinkedIn and webhook steps, and replies land in Unibox with AI reply labels. Inbox Placement sits in its product menu under Deliverability & Infrastructure alongside AirMail and Email Accounts. The Outreach page's button reads "Start for free".


## Smartlead


Smartlead's pricing page lists four plans. Base at $39 a month covers 2,000 contacts, 6,000 email sends and 2,000 verified prospect emails. Pro at $94 moves to 30,000 contacts and 90,000 sends. Smart at $174 and Prime at $379 remove the contact cap and allow 150,000 and 500,000 sends respectively, and Prime includes three SmartServers, Smartlead's dedicated sending servers. Yearly billing lists $32.50, $78.30, $144.50 and $314.60. The pricing page offers a free trial where you pick a plan later and advertises 50% off the first month.


*Smartlead's pricing page, as of October 3, 2026.*


Smartlead is the most explicit of these tools about placement testing, and it charges for it separately. SmartDelivery starts at $49 a month for 120 campaign sequence tests with up to 50 sender accounts per test, with $174 and $599 tiers above. Mailboxes are sold through SmartSenders from $4.50 per mailbox per month and $13 per domain per year, and SmartServers are $39 per server per month. The second channel on Smartlead's homepage is calls, through SmartDialer. If you leave Woodpecker to push raw email volume through many mailboxes and want dedicated servers on the menu, Smartlead fits that shape.


## lemlist


lemlist's pricing page lists an Email plan at $69 a month ($55 yearly) with unlimited users and email senders and 50,000 emails a month, and a Multichannel plan at $109 a month ($87 yearly) with unlimited emails and messages, LinkedIn automation, SMS, a WhatsApp add-on and a built-in dialer. Enterprise is custom. The 14-day free trial runs on Multichannel features, minus in-app calls, with 200 lead-finding credits. Lead data enrichment and buying intent signals are paid add-ons at $20 and $29 a month.


*lemlist's pricing page, as of October 3, 2026.*


Of the tools here, lemlist is the closest match to Woodpecker plus its LinkedIn add-on, since LinkedIn visits, follows, invites, messages, voice messages and InMail all appear in the Multichannel feature list. The deliverability column of the feature table lists warm-up, a DNS setup test, deliverability testing, sending limit management, inbox rotation, deliverability alerts and in-app domain and email purchase. AI reply intent detection and out-of-office detection sort the unified inbox. The Multichannel plan is shown as a per-user figure with five senders per user, so a five-person team should compare that against Woodpecker's unlimited members plus five LinkedIn accounts at $29 each. If lemlist is already on your shortlist, our[lemlist alternatives roundup](https://supersend.io/blog/lemlist-alternatives) compares it against a different set of tools.


## Mailshake


Mailshake's pricing page lists Starter at $29 a month ($25 yearly) with one email address, 1,500 sends a month, unlimited uploaded contacts, unlimited warmup and unlimited email verification. Email Outreach at $49 ($45 yearly) raises that to two email addresses and unlimited sends, and adds email rotation, a unified inbox and Salesforce, Pipedrive and HubSpot integrations. Sales Engagement at $99 ($85 yearly) allows ten email addresses, adds five phone numbers and a power dialer, and includes a one-on-one onboarding call. An Agency plan with unlimited email addresses is sold through sales. Data Finder is $19 a month and Ready to Use Mailboxes are $12 a month.


*Mailshake's pricing page, as of October 3, 2026.*


Two things set Mailshake apart from everything else on this page. It has no free trial: the pricing FAQ says payment is collected up front, with concierge onboarding and deliverability training offered instead. And its multichannel story centres on calls, with the homepage listing a dialer and a Social Automation feature for multi-channel social selling. Email Deliverability appears as a feature in its own right. Mailshake fits a solo founder who wants the lowest flat monthly price for email only and is comfortable paying before trying.


## Saleshandy


Saleshandy's pricing page lists Starter at $41 a month ($34 yearly) for one user, 2,000 active prospects, 6,000 emails a month, unlimited connected email accounts and 1,500 lead finder credits. Pro at $99 ($76 yearly) covers ten users, 30,000 active prospects, 100,000 emails and 4,000 credits. Scale at $189 ($149 yearly) removes the user and active-prospect caps and allows 200,000 emails. Enterprise is custom and adds SSO and agency whitelabel. The trial is seven days with no card.


*Saleshandy's pricing page, as of October 3, 2026.*


Saleshandy's distinction is "active prospects": you can store as many prospects as you like, and the cap applies only to those sitting in live sequences. That is a gentler version of Woodpecker's contacted-prospect count. The pricing page describes sequences spanning email, calls, LinkedIn and WhatsApp plus manual tasks, though the channel icons it shows are Email, Call, WhatsApp and Tasks, so check in the trial how LinkedIn steps actually execute. Inbox Placement is listed as an add-on, and its own mailboxes start at $2.99 per mailbox per month on an annual commitment, with SPF, DKIM and DMARC preconfigured. Subsequences trigger follow-up sequences based on how prospects respond.


## SuperSend


SuperSend prices on emails sent, with unlimited contacts on every plan and every feature on every plan. Plans start from $59 a month: Starter is $59 for 15,000 emails and one LinkedIn sender, Growth is $99 for 50,000 emails and two LinkedIn senders, and Scale is $319 for 200,000 emails and five LinkedIn senders. Yearly billing is about 15% off, which works out to $50, $84 and $271 a month. Email over the plan limit is billed per email on monthly plans at $0.006 on Starter, $0.004 on Growth and $0.0025 on Scale. Extra LinkedIn senders are $29 a month, the same per-account figure Woodpecker charges for its LinkedIn add-on. The full breakdown is on the[SuperSend pricing page](https://supersend.io/pricing) . Signup is free with no card; a seven-day trial with a card on file starts when you launch a campaign or turn on warmup.


Email and LinkedIn steps run in one sequence on one contact record, so a reply on either channel stops both, which is the behavior you otherwise have to reconcile by hand when email and LinkedIn live in two tools. The[LinkedIn outreach feature page](https://supersend.io/features/linkedin-outreach) shows how the LinkedIn steps sit inside the sequence builder. The deliverability pieces sit next to the campaigns: warmup on each mailbox, SPF/DKIM/DMARC checks, bounce monitoring and placement tests against seed inboxes, all described on the[deliverability monitoring page](https://supersend.io/features/deliverability) . Replies from every sending mailbox land in one inbox, labeled by AI, with interested replies on top. You can connect Google or Outlook inboxes you already own or buy domains and inboxes inside the app. Bought inboxes are $5 a month each and domains are $13 a year, both set up with SPF, DKIM and DMARC. A default placement test checks 10 seed inboxes, always including Google and Outlook, and runs on plan credits at 5 credits per seed (50 per default test). A campaign pauses itself when its invalid-recipient bounce rate goes over 3% (adjustable per campaign) after 100 or more sends, and small campaigns pause after 10 invalid-recipient bounces. The default daily send cap is 15 emails per mailbox per day, adjustable per mailbox. SuperSend fits a founder or small team that wants Woodpecker's email-plus-LinkedIn shape at a flat volume price with placement testing included rather than bolted on.


## Which one to pick


- **You want email volume and nothing else, at the lowest flat price:** Mailshake Starter at $29 a month, if 1,500 sends and one mailbox are enough and you accept paying without a trial. Smartlead Base at $39 gives 6,000 sends with a trial.
- **You run very high volume across many mailboxes and want dedicated infrastructure:** Smartlead Prime with its SmartServers, or Instantly Light Speed with SISR. Both put placement testing and infrastructure on the menu; Smartlead charges for SmartDelivery separately.
- **You want LinkedIn, SMS, WhatsApp and calls in one sequence and have a bigger per-seat budget:** lemlist Multichannel.
- **You want a gentler prospect cap than Woodpecker's and a short no-card trial:** Saleshandy, whose active-prospect model only counts people in live sequences.
- **You want Woodpecker's email-plus-LinkedIn shape, flat email-volume pricing, unlimited contacts and placement tests included:** SuperSend, with Growth at $99 as the usual starting plan.


Run whichever you shortlist through the same first test. Connect one mailbox, turn on warmup, send a placement test, and read the result before a single prospect sees a message. A tool that makes that hard is telling you where deliverability sits in its priorities. Our[cold email deliverability checklist](https://supersend.io/blog/cold-email-deliverability-checklist) walks through what to check between connecting the mailbox and launching.


## FAQ


**What is the cheapest Woodpecker alternative for cold email?** Among flat monthly plans listed on these tools' pricing pages, Mailshake Starter at $29 a month is the lowest, capped at 1,500 sends and one email address, with no free trial. Smartlead Base at $39 and Saleshandy Starter at $41 each allow 6,000 emails a month. Woodpecker itself charges $7.00 per 100 contacted prospects at the lowest tier, so 500 prospects comes to $35 a month, and a small list that you contact once can be cheap there too.


**Which Woodpecker alternatives include LinkedIn steps?** lemlist on its Multichannel plan, Instantly according to its Outreach page, Saleshandy according to its pricing page description, and SuperSend on every plan. Smartlead's homepage lists calls through SmartDialer as its second channel, and Mailshake's homepage lists a dialer and Social Automation for multi-channel social selling.


**Which tools include inbox placement testing?** Smartlead sells it as the SmartDelivery add-on from $49 a month. lemlist lists deliverability testing in its feature table. Saleshandy lists Inbox Placement as an add-on. Instantly lists Inbox Placement as a product. SuperSend includes placement tests against seed inboxes alongside campaigns, paid for in plan credits. Woodpecker's pricing page lists a domain audit and free warm-up among its key features, and Mailshake's site lists Email Deliverability as a feature.


**Do I have to buy mailboxes from the tool, or can I use my own?** Every tool here connects mailboxes you already own: Woodpecker and Instantly list unlimited email accounts, Smartlead lists your own email network via private OAuth, lemlist lists Google, Microsoft and SMTP, Mailshake lists mail accounts from any provider, Saleshandy lists unlimited sending mailboxes with no per-inbox fee, and SuperSend connects your Google or Outlook inboxes. All seven also sell mailboxes in-app. Priced per mailbox per month on their pricing pages: Woodpecker $6 (Google or Microsoft), Smartlead $4.50 (Google or Outlook), Mailshake $12, Saleshandy $2.99 billed annually, and SuperSend $5 plus $13 a year per domain. Instantly lists Email Accounts and AirMail, and lemlist lists in-app domain and email purchase.


**Which of these have a free trial?** lemlist offers 14 days. Woodpecker offers 14 days or 100 cold emails, whichever comes first, with no card. Saleshandy offers 7 days with no card. Smartlead offers a free trial where you pick a plan afterwards. Instantly's Outreach page button reads "Start for free". SuperSend signup is free with no card and the 7-day trial begins when you launch a campaign or turn on warmup. Mailshake has no trial and collects payment up front.
